response.justification: Experienced, versatile senior engineer with genuine geospatial credentials (GISCollective, Green Map web GIS, FOSS4G talk) and some low-latency distributed systems work at Sociomantic handling millions of requests per second. However, the core requirement — modern C++ (or Rust) in commercial/open-source settings — is essentially unmet: the only C/C++ exposure is a ~7-month stint at National Instruments in 2014-2015 plus a university thesis project, with no Rust at all. The last decade is dominated by TypeScript/Node.js and D, and there is no experience with routing tiles, map data pipelines, or navigation guidance QA. Could be worth a conversation given the systems mindset and geospatial passion, but they would be a significant ramp-up risk against candidates with current C++ pipeline experience.
strengths: Deep, sustained geospatial/GIS domain experience through GISCollective and Green Map
Low-latency, high-throughput backend work with async I/O, fibers, and caching at Sociomantic
Strong engineering discipline: TDD, CI/CD, testing tooling authorship, and proven cross-stack adaptability
concerns: Modern C++ experience is minimal and over a decade old; no Rust experience listed
Recent roles are web/full-stack (TypeScript, Node.js), not systems or data-pipeline engineering
No exposure to routing tiling, map data pipelines, real-time traffic integration, or navigation QA
